title: Minimum Cost to Connect Ropes
statement: You are given a list of positive integers, each the length of a rope. Connecting two ropes fuses them into a single rope whose length is the sum of the two, and the cost of that connection equals that sum. You must keep connecting ropes until only one rope remains, and you want the total connection cost to be as small as possible. Return the minimum possible total cost as an integer. If the list has fewer than two ropes there is nothing to connect, so return 0. The minimum total cost is uniquely determined regardless of how ties between equal-length ropes are broken, so no tie-break rule on the order of connections is needed.
reference_solution:
import heapq


def min_connect_cost(ropes):
    if len(ropes) < 2:
        return 0
    heap = list(ropes)
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    total = 0
    while len(heap) > 1:
        a = heapq.heappop(heap)
        b = heapq.heappop(heap)
        combined = a + b
        total += combined
        heapq.heappush(heap, combined)
    return total
hints: At every step you only ever need the two shortest ropes available right now -- which data structure hands you the current minimum cheaply and lets you add new items back?
Keep the rope lengths in a min-heap. Each round pop the two smallest, and remember that the rope you create by fusing them must go back into the heap so it can be chosen again later.

Heapify the lengths, then loop while more than one rope remains: pop two, let combined = a + b, add combined to a running total, and push combined back. When one rope is left, the accumulated total (the sum of every fusion) is the answer; return 0 up front if there are fewer than two ropes.
